identificationModule.briefTitle: The Effect of Supraglottic and Oropharyngeal Decontamination on the Incidence of Ventilator-associated Pneumonia
identificationModule.officialTitle: The Effect of Supraglottic and Oropharyngeal Decontamination on the Incidence of Ventilator-associated Pneumonia and Associated Microbiomes.

descriptionModule.briefSummary: Oropharynx is the main source of pathogen microorganisms for the ventilator - associated pneumoniae. As known bacteriophages can eliminate different pathogen microorganisms or reduce a degree of a pathogen's colonization. The research team is considering that oropharyngeal decontamination with bacteriophages can prevent the developing of the ventilator - associated pneumoniae. There will be three groups in this investigation: placebo, antiseptic drug (Octenisept) and bacteriophage (Sexthaphag).

interventions.name: Control
interventions.description: Oropharyngeal decontamination with saline will be performing three time a day every 8 hours during mechanical ventilation

interventions.name: Antiseptic Solution
interventions.description: Oropharyngeal decontamination with antiseptic solution will be performing three time a day every 8 hours during mechanical ventilation

interventions.name: Bacteriophage
interventions.description: Oropharyngeal decontamination with bacteriophage will be performing three time a day every 8 hours during mechanical ventilation

primaryOutcomes.description: CPIS is using for diagnosis the VAP, if CPIS equal or more 6, the VAP will be confirmed
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Change from Baseline CPIS at 14 days

primaryOutcomes.measure: Changing of oral and lung microbiomes
primaryOutcomes.description: Microbiology researching samples from oral cavity and trachea. The Gram positive and Gram negative aerobes and anaerobes will be assessed with observing Colony Form Unit
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Change from Baseline Microbiology researching at 14 days

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

\- invasive mechanical ventilation beyond 48 hours

Exclusion Criteria:

* hospital - acquired pneumonia
* community - acquired pneumoniae
* BMI \> 35 kg/cm2
* pregnancy
* tracheostomy
* reintubation
